title: Battle of Cowpens, 17 January 1781
subtitle: Morgan's three lines and the double envelopment of Tarleton

about: Unit positions come from the Revolutionary War workbook (the Cowpens rows), built from Morgan's report, Tarleton's and Howard's accounts, the journals and memoirs of men in the ranks, the Army's 1996 staff ride handbook, the Army War College study of 1928 and the National Park Service's handbook and waysides. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.

No map made at the time shows this ground, and the accounts give distances, not places. Every unit is therefore placed by distance along the Green River Road, which still crosses the field, counted from the spot where Tarleton's column came out of the woods. Lines may be 50 to 100 m from where they really stood; none is rated better than medium.

The clock follows the staff ride's maps: first shots about 07:00, the end about 07:50. Eyewitnesses say only "about sunrise", which was at 07:07; one Army study puts everything an hour later. Tap a unit to see the range of times its record allows.
Solid symbols are positions a source gives. Dashed symbols are worked out or are the last position on record. A question mark means the place is doubtful.
Symbols are blue for the Americans and red for the British and Loyalist troops. Zoom in to see Pickens's line by its regiments and Howard's by its parts.

The current map is the US Geological Survey's topographic map, and Satellite its aerial photography, both streamed from the USGS. If they cannot be reached, a simplified drawing of OpenStreetMap roads and streams is shown instead.

Where the sources disagree (the hour, the numbers, which riflemen were on the right, how far Howard fell back, who brought the militia back), the workbook's Hypotheses sheet gives each reading and says which one the playback follows.

The playback opens on "1781 with terrain", a reconstruction: the roads Edwin Bearss drew in 1967 as the roads of the battle, laid on the ground by the road the park still keeps, and today's ground, which the park has kept open. The map details (the i button) list each road with its source and how sure it is, and offer the other maps of this ground: Bearss's own maps phase by phase, the Army War College sketches of 1928, the USGS maps of 1959 and 1975, Mills's map of 1825 and the park map.

No town or village stood near the Cowpens in 1781: Spartanburg was laid out in 1785, Gaffney in the 1800s, the town of Cowpens in 1880. The nearest places named in the campaign are shown at the edge of the map, with an arrow and their distance in a straight line from the middle of the screen: Gilbert Town in North Carolina (the Rutherford County seat, where Ferguson camped before Kings Mountain), Charlotte (the village Cornwallis held in the autumn of 1780), Winnsborough (Cornwallis's winter camp, which he left on 8 January) and Ninety Six (the British post Morgan was sent to threaten).

terrain.about: In the United States these tiles come from the USGS's National Elevation Dataset, a survey of the bare ground with no buildings or trees in it. Bumps narrower than about 20 m are taken off and the rest smoothed over about 20 m. Heights are in metres, good to a metre or two. This is today's ground: the park keeps the field open, but SC 11, the park roads and the visitor centre have cut into it since 1781.
terrain.beyond: Beyond the dotted line the roads of 1781 stop: only today's relief and contours are drawn there, so the map fills the window.

opening.label: Before daylight
opening.text: Before daylight on 17 January 1781. Daniel Morgan's detachment is in camp at the Cowpens, a well-known pasture ground on the Green River Road. Banastre Tarleton, sent by Cornwallis to destroy it, has been marching since three in the morning and is five miles off. Morgan has chosen to stand here. Press play: the units come onto the map as they form.

sides.name: British Crown forces (British regulars and Loyalist provincials)

units.name: Morgan's detachment (the "flying army")
units.label: Morgan
units.notes: The whole American force. Its strength is disputed by a factor of two: CH03.

assignments.strength: "We fought only eight hundred men, two-thirds of which were militia" (S96). 1,117 by the staff ride's charts: Howard 350, Pickens 650, cavalry 117 (S95, pp. 92-94). "Some 830" (S104). Tarleton counted about 1,920 (S97).

units.name: Morgan's headquarters
units.label: Morgan (HQ)
units.notes: Aide Maj. Edward Giles and brigade major Capt. Brookes are named in Morgan's report (S96).

units.name: Howard's line: the Continental light infantry and the Virginians (the main line)
units.label: Howard
units.notes: The third and main line. The staff ride calls it the Delaware-Maryland Regiment (+).

assignments.strength: "About 350 men" (Howard, S98; S95, p. 92). Under 450 (S103, p. 67). Mackenzie says 250 Continentals; Tarleton 500 (S95, p. 92 n. 5).

units.name: Maryland and Delaware light infantry (Continentals)
units.label: MD and DE Continentals
units.notes: Picked men of the two Maryland regiments with the Delaware company (S98). Companies on the staff ride's chart: Beatty (MD), Kirkwood (DE), Anderson, Dobson (MD) (S95, p. 92).

assignments.strength: About 320 Continentals (S104, Prologue by George Scheer, before p. 12). Formed in two ranks over about 200 yards (S95, p. 48).

units.name: Kirkwood's Delaware company
units.label: Kirkwood
units.notes: Not placed on the map: no source read says where in the line it stood. It "wheeled to the right and attacked their left flank" (Seymour, S100).

units.name: Wallace's Virginia company
units.label: Wallace
units.notes: The right of Howard's line. "Virginia regulars" to Howard (S98); Virginia militia on the staff ride's chart (S95, p. 92). Its attempt to change front began the retreat.

units.name: Triplett's and Tate's Virginia militia
units.label: Triplett and Tate
units.notes: Two companies of Virginia riflemen, many of them former Continentals; Buchanan's Augusta men with Tate (S96; Neel, S101). Which flank they held is disputed: CH06. Ward (S92, p. 757) splits them: Tate on Howard's right, Triplett on his left; recorded under CH06.

units.name: Pickens's militia (the second line)
units.label: Pickens
units.notes: Volunteers of North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia. Pickens did not command them all, but they served in his line (S95, p. 93 n. 7). Maj. James Jackson of Georgia acted as brigade major.

assignments.strength: 650 (S95, p. 93). Tarleton took the line for "about one thousand" (S97).

units.name: McDowell's North Carolina riflemen (skirmishers)
units.label: McDowell
units.notes: Half of the skirmish line. On the right by Morgan's report, on the left by Hammond's notes: CH05. Ward calls him Joseph on p. 752 and 'Major Charles McDowell' on p. 757.

units.name: Cunningham's Georgians (skirmishers)
units.label: Cunningham
units.notes: The other half of the skirmish line, with the dismounted part of McCall's state troops under Maj. Samuel Hammond (S99). On the left by Morgan's report: CH05.

units.name: Brandon's regiment (South Carolina militia)
units.label: Brandon
units.notes: With Lt. Col. William Farr. "A column marches up in front of Brandon's men" (McJunkin, S101).

units.name: Hays's regiment (South Carolina militia)
units.label: Hays
units.notes: Morgan writes "Hay".

units.name: McCall's South Carolina state troops (dismounted part)
units.label: McCall
units.notes: The part of McCall's regiment not yet equipped as dragoons, under Maj. Samuel Hammond (S99); Morgan lists "McCall" on the left of the line (S96).

units.name: Roebuck's battalion (South Carolina militia)
units.label: Roebuck
units.notes: On the staff ride's chart and in McJunkin's list; no source read says where in the line it stood. Not placed.

units.name: Washington's cavalry (the reserve)
units.label: Washington
units.notes: The 3d Continental Light Dragoons with McCall's mounted volunteers.

assignments.strength: About 117: 72 dragoons and 45 mounted militia (S95, p. 94). Tarleton saw 120 (S97).

units.name: 3d Continental Light Dragoons
units.label: 3d Light Dragoons
units.notes: Troops under Fauntleroy and Jones on the staff ride's chart (S95, p. 94). Drawn as part of Washington's cavalry.

assignments.strength: 72, counted by Josiah Martin on 16 January (S95, p. 94 n. 10)

units.name: McCall's mounted volunteers
units.label: McCall (mounted)
units.notes: Enrolled as dragoons the night before the battle and given sabres (McJunkin, S101; S103, pp. 64-65). Drawn as part of Washington's cavalry.

units.name: Tarleton's detachment
units.label: Tarleton
units.notes: The whole British force. See CH04 for its strength.

assignments.strength: 1,126 (S95, p. 91). Morgan: "not less than one thousand one hundred and fifty" with the baggage guard; "their own officers confess that they fought one thousand and thirty-seven" (S96). About 1,100 (S104).

units.name: Light infantry (companies of the 16th, the 71st and the Prince of Wales's American Regiment)
units.label: Light infantry
units.notes: The right of the British line. One of its companies was provincial (the Prince of Wales's American Regiment).

assignments.commander: Not named in the sources read
assignments.strength: 150 (S95, p. 91). The light company of the 71st alone was 69 on the return of 15 January (S95, p. 91 n. 3).

units.name: British Legion infantry
units.label: Legion infantry
units.notes: The centre of the British line. Provincials raised in the middle colonies; many of them prisoners enlisted after Camden (S95, p. 56).

assignments.commander: Not named in the sources read
assignments.strength: 300 (S95, p. 91). The whole Legion, horse and foot, was 451 on the return of 15 January (S95, p. 91 n. 1).

units.name: 7th Regiment of Foot (Royal Fusiliers), 1st Battalion
units.label: 7th Fusiliers
units.notes: The left of the British line. Mostly recruits (S95, p. 76).

assignments.strength: 176: 167 rank and file and 9 officers (S95, p. 91 n. 4)

units.name: 71st Regiment of Foot (Fraser's Highlanders), 1st Battalion
units.label: 71st Highlanders
units.notes: The reserve, then the left of the attack on Howard.

assignments.strength: 200 (Tarleton; S95, p. 91). 249 on the return of 15 January (S95, p. 91 n. 3).

units.name: Royal Artillery: 3-pounder with the right of the line
units.label: 3-pdr (right)
units.notes: One of two light 3-pounders ("grasshoppers"). The first part of the line advanced "under the fire of a 3-pounder" (S97). Ward's text (S92, p. 758) has the guns in the centre and on the left; his own map (p. 759) has them in the gaps either side of the Legion, as drawn.

assignments.commander: Not named in the sources read
assignments.strength: About 20 gunners for the two guns (S95, p. 91); Babits says 36 (S95, p. 91 n. 2)

units.name: Royal Artillery: 3-pounder with the 7th Regiment
units.label: 3-pdr (left)
units.notes: "The other 3-pounder was given to the right division of the 7th" (S97).

assignments.commander: Not named in the sources read

units.name: 17th Light Dragoons (troop)
units.label: 17th Light Dragoons
units.notes: The dragoons on the right flank (S95, p. 76), who rode down the militia and were met by Washington (Simmons, S101).

assignments.commander: A captain (S97); not named in the sources read

units.name: British Legion cavalry: Ogilvie's advance guard
units.label: Ogilvie
units.notes: Two troops sent ahead before dawn; then the fifty dragoons on the left flank (S95, p. 76).

units.name: British Legion cavalry (the reserve)
units.label: Legion cavalry
units.notes: In reserve with the 71st. It would not charge and left the field (S97).

assignments.strength: "Near two hundred cavalry" in reserve (S97); 250 Legion cavalry in all (S95, p. 91); Mackenzie puts all the British cavalry at 350 (S95, p. 91 n. 1)

units.name: Baggage and its guard
units.label: Baggage
units.notes: Left on the ground of the night's camp till daybreak "under the protection of a detachment of each corps" (S97), about twelve miles from the field (S96); under Lt. Fraser of the 71st (S95, p. 85). Off the map; not placed.

steps.place: Morgan's camp at the Cowpens, on the Green River Road north-west of the field
steps.quote: S96: "An hour before daylight one of my scouts returned and informed me that Lieut. Col. Tarleton had advanced within five miles of our camp." S100 (Anderson): "Before day Reced Information ... We got up and put Ourselves in Order of Battle by day Light".
steps.time_basis: Before the fighting: "an hour before daylight" for the warning and "by day Light" for the line (S96; S100). The clock times are estimates from sunrise at 0707 (S95, p. 67 n. 28).

location.basis: Placed by distance along the Historic Green River Road as OpenStreetMap draws it (S39), counted from the south-east end of the Battlefield Trail loop (35.13294, -81.81012), where the staff ride's Vantage 6 (S95, p. 77) and the NPS wayside "The British Army" (S105) put the head of Tarleton's column as it came onto the field. About 555 m up the road and 375 m north-east of it, in a ravine: measured on Bearss's Plate I, which draws the camp level with the main line and off the road to the north-east, and his text puts it "in a wooded ravine, about 1,000 yards northwest of the cabin of Robert Scruggs" (S107, p. 8). The staff ride puts it about 300 m north of its Vantage 1 (S95, p. 72), some 500 m from here: not reconciled.

steps.notes: Morgan reached the Cowpens "about sundown" on 16 January (S95, p. 46). The place of the camp is the least sure point on the map. Audit of 24 Nov 2026: moved from the road 1 km up it to where Bearss draws the camp.

steps.quote: S98 (Howard): Morgan "ordered me to keep with the men, until we came to the rising ground near Washington's horse; and he rode forward to fix on the most proper place for us to halt and face about."

events.name: Morgan forms for battle
events.text: About an hour before daylight a scout reports Tarleton within five miles. Morgan turns his men out and puts them in three lines across the Green River Road: riflemen in front, Pickens's militia behind them, and Howard's Continentals and Virginians on the rise behind, with Washington's cavalry in reserve.

events.name: The pickets are driven in
events.label: Pickets driven in
events.text: About day, Tarleton's advance guard of Legion dragoons drives in Capt. Inman's mounted pickets on the Green River Road and finds the Americans drawn up to fight.

events.name: Tarleton deploys
events.text: The British come out of the woods and form one line in sight of the Americans: light infantry on the right, the Legion infantry in the centre, the 7th Fusiliers on the left, a 3-pounder in each gap and fifty dragoons on each flank. The 71st Highlanders and about 200 Legion cavalry stand in reserve 150 yards back.

events.name: First shots
events.text: Tarleton sends Ogilvie's Legion dragoons to drive in the riflemen in front. The riflemen fire from behind the trees and the dragoons come back with empty saddles. Militia veterans gave John Savage of Brandon's regiment the first shot.

events.name: The British line advances
events.label: The line advances
events.text: About sunrise the two guns open and the whole line comes on with three cheers. Morgan answers along the militia line: "They gave us the British halloo, boys, give them the Indian halloo."

events.name: The skirmishers fall back
events.text: McDowell's and Cunningham's riflemen, having picked off officers at long range, fall back on Pickens's line.

events.name: The militia volleys
events.text: Pickens's militia hold their fire until the British are within killing distance, then fire by regiments: "pop, pop, pop, and then a whole volley". The British line halts to dress and comes on again.

events.name: The militia withdraw; dragoons ride them down
events.label: Militia withdraw
events.text: As ordered, the militia file off round Howard's line, most of them round its left, to re-form in rear. The 17th Light Dragoons on Tarleton's right charge after them towards their horses; Washington's cavalry strikes the dragoons and drives them back.

events.name: Line against line
events.text: The British infantry close on Howard's line and the two fire at close range, neither giving way. Tarleton orders up the 71st on his left to turn Howard's right, and the reserve cavalry to follow it; the cavalry does not come.

events.name: Howard's line falls back
events.label: Howard falls back
events.text: Howard orders his right company to face the Highlanders. The order goes wrong; the company faces about, and the rest of the line, taking it for a retreat, marches to the rear in good order. Morgan picks the ground for it to halt, about 80 to 100 yards back.

events.name: Face about: volley and bayonet
events.label: Volley and bayonet
events.text: The British, sure the day is won, rush on out of order. At 10 to 30 yards Howard's line faces about and fires; then it charges with the bayonet. The British line stops, breaks and runs.

events.name: Double envelopment
events.text: Washington's cavalry rides round the British right and into their rear; Pickens's militia come back into the fight round the American right, onto the 71st. The infantry throw down their arms. The gunners fight to the last by their two 3-pounders, which are taken.

events.name: Tarleton's last charge
events.text: The Legion cavalry will not charge and about 200 of them leave the field. Tarleton leads some fifty horsemen, most of them of the 17th Light Dragoons, at the American cavalry and is beaten off; he and Washington cross swords before he rides away down the Green River Road.

events.name: Pursuit
events.text: Washington and Pickens follow Tarleton for 22 to 24 miles without catching him; the British burn most of their baggage. Morgan counts over 500 prisoners, two guns and two colours for 12 killed and about 60 wounded, and marches off the field the same day to get the prisoners away from Cornwallis.

reconstructions.title: The Carolinas, 1775 to 1781: a WarMapper reconstruction
reconstructions.label: 1775 (reconstructed)
reconstructions.about: This is a WarMapper reconstruction, not a period map. Its lines are those of Henry Mouzon's map of the two Carolinas (1775), laid on today's ground: the rivers and the sea coast fitted to today's courses, which they keep, and the main roads and boundary lines carried with them. Mouzon's map was made for the colonies' trade and land grants, not as a survey: his roads are good to a few kilometres, his up-country less. South Carolina is traced at the level of its main lines; North Carolina (since 27 Nov 2026) only for the ground of the campaign of 1781, from Charlotte and Salisbury to Guilford, Hillsborough, Halifax and the Dan. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.
reconstructions.note: Rivers and coast good to about 1-2 km where today's river is in Natural Earth; roads and boundaries to 3-5 km; the far north-west to no better than 10 km. In North Carolina nine towns hold the fit, each found again 1.3-6.6 km from its site when left out. Not yet traced: inlets, islands and sounds, swamps, the lesser roads, ferries and fords; in North Carolina the Neuse, the Tar and the sounds (east of 77 W, beyond the sheet), the rivers and roads of the mountains and of the east, and Mouzon's towns other than those named. Guilford Court House is not on Mouzon's map (it was built in 1774): its name is placed where the battle's playback has it.
reconstructions.credit: WarMapper reconstruction from Mouzon, 1775 (Library of Congress), fitted with Natural Earth; North Carolina checked against Collet, 1770 (Library of Congress)

layers.title: Rivers, as Mouzon draws them (1775), fitted to today's courses
layers.how: Picked by hand every 50-100 pixels of a half-resolution crop and snapped by program to the engraved line; fitted to the ground by matching them to today's rivers (Natural Earth). Rivers with no line in Natural Earth (Pacolet, Tyger, Enoree, Black, Ashley, Combahee), and since the refit of 26 Nov 2026 the Pee Dee, Little Pee Dee and Waccamaw, follow the fit and are low. Each river is one line, joined across the strips where the scan's mounted sections meet (2-6 km). North Carolina (27 Nov 2026): the Catawba and Broad above the 1772 line, the Yadkin to the Pee Dee, the Haw with Reedy Fork and Troublesome Creek, the Deep, the Cape Fear, the Dan and the Roanoke, picked and snapped the same way and matched to Natural Earth (Reedy Fork and Troublesome Creek, which it lacks, follow the fit and are low).

Mouzon draws it from the Savannah at a corner tree, past DeWitt's Corner, to a corner tree on the Reedy River and north to the 1772 line. The Cherokee ceded the land east of it in 1766-67 and nearly all the rest in South Carolina at DeWitt's Corner, 20 May 1777, so it is drawn until then.

reconstructions.title: The Cowpens, January 1781: a WarMapper reconstruction
reconstructions.label: 1781 (reconstructed)
reconstructions.about: This is a WarMapper reconstruction, not a period map: no map of 1781 shows this ground. The roads are those Edwin Bearss drew in 1967 as the roads of the battle, laid on the ground by the road the park still keeps, and beyond his sheet the roads of the 1959 survey on the lines Mills's map of 1825 gives. The ground is today's, which the park has kept much as it was; the streams are today's. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.
reconstructions.note: Inside Bearss's sheet the roads are good to about 25-50 m: his road matches the park's trace to 4 m at the median, and his other roads lie within 20-50 m of the roads of 1959. Beyond it they are roads of 1959 (and, for Tarleton's approach, today's Green River Road), rated low. Bearss shows no other roads, houses or fields; the ground was open woods, pastured, with no undergrowth (S107, p. 8).
reconstructions.credit: WarMapper reconstruction from Bearss, 1967 (National Park Service), the USGS sheets of 1959 and 1975, and Mills, 1825

features.name: Mill Gap road
features.desc: The Mill Gap road (today the Historic Green River Road) through the field
features.basis: The park's trace of the road, as OpenStreetMap draws it (S39). Bearss draws the road of the battle here (S107, Plate I): fitted to the ground, his road lies 4 m from the trace at the median, 15 m at the 90th percentile. The 1975 photo map (S109) shows the old road bed on the same line, and SC 11 ran on it in 1959 (S108).

A road of the 1959 sheet (S108) and a track on the 1975 photo map (S109) lie on the same line. Landers (1928) draws his "Old Mill Gap Road" some 20 degrees further south.
